focus: Backend spot-check: 5 critical backend requirements + confirm backend unchanged from qa-run-1
methodology: Ran `diff` between qa-run-1/diff.txt and qa-run-2/diff.txt. Confirmed all backend Ruby files are byte-identical. The only additions in qa-run-2 are: (1) ChannelMessageListItem.tsx frontend fix (adding subject: '' to channelMessageTemplate prop), (2) db/schema.rb (auto-generated schema dump after migration ran, was absent from qa-run-1 diff). Then spot-checked the 5 critical backend requirements against the diff.
backend_identity_details: All backend .rb files in qa-run-2 diff are identical to qa-run-1 diff. The `diff` command shows only two additions: ChannelMessageListItem.tsx (frontend fix) and db/schema.rb (schema dump). No backend file was modified, added, or removed between runs.

spot_checks.spec_reference: Spec: 'update ChannelMessageMailer#notify_candidate to read channel_message.subject and fall back to the current hardcoded literal when the stored subject is blank'
spot_checks.reasoning: The mailer reads @channel_message.subject, uses .presence (returns nil for blank/nil strings), and falls back to the exact hardcoded literal that was previously the only subject. This matches the spec requirement precisely.

spot_checks.spec_reference: Spec: 'Rename the existing CustomChannelMessageBodyValidator to CustomChannelMessageValidator and apply it to subject the same way it is currently applied to body.'
spot_checks.diff_content_model_usage: validates :body, custom_channel_message: true / validates :subject, custom_channel_message: true
spot_checks.reasoning: File renamed from custom_channel_message_body_validator.rb to custom_channel_message_validator.rb. Class renamed from CustomChannelMessageBodyValidator to CustomChannelMessageValidator. Model (channel_message.rb) updated: old `validates :body, custom_channel_message_body: true` replaced with `validates :body, custom_channel_message: true` and new `validates :subject, custom_channel_message: true` added. Matches spec exactly.

spot_checks.spec_reference: Spec (architecture): subject threads through all 7 channel_message creation paths including bulk
spot_checks.diff_content: Hand-built hash at line 9 adds `subject: bulk_channel_message_params[:subject]`. Strong params at line 18 adds :subject to permit list. Sanitization at line 20 adds `next_params[:subject] = sanitize(next_params[:subject]) if next_params.key?(:subject)`.
spot_checks.reasoning: All three touchpoints in BulkChannelMessagesController are present: (1) hand-built hash includes subject from params, (2) strong params permits :subject, (3) sanitize call parallels the existing body sanitization pattern. Complete threading.

spot_checks.requirement: 4. parse_text rename in both CreateStageAutomationMessage and BulkChannelMessageSendJob
spot_checks.spec_reference: Spec: 'Rename the existing private parse_body methods in CreateStageAutomationMessage (interactor) and BulkChannelMessageSendJob (job) in place to parse_text.'

BulkChannelMessageSendJob.new: channel_message_params = params.merge(body: parse_text(user, job_application, params[:body]), subject: parse_text(user, job_application, params[:subject]))
BulkChannelMessageSendJob.method_rename: def parse_body(user, job_application, params) -> def parse_text(user, job_application, text)

spot_checks.reasoning: Both files rename parse_body to parse_text. Both generalize the method to accept a text parameter instead of reading from params[:body] internally. Both add a blank guard (return '' if text.blank?). Both call sites now pass subject through the same method as body. The different signatures are preserved (interactor: parse_text(text); job: parse_text(user, job_application, text)). Matches spec exactly, including the note that 'No further refactor' and 'they have different signatures'.

spot_checks.spec_reference: Spec: 'Add the same two text_replacer calls over subject so candidate names don't persist in stored subjects after an anonymization run.'
spot_checks.diff_content: channel_message.subject = text_replacer(channel_message.subject, real_first_name, name_replacement) / channel_message.subject = text_replacer(channel_message.subject, real_last_name, name_replacement)
spot_checks.reasoning: Two text_replacer calls on subject (one for first name, one for last name) added immediately after the existing body field replacements and before channel_message.save!. Parallels the exact pattern used for body, body_legacy_markdown, body_raw_html, body_plain_text, and body_sanitized_html. Matches spec exactly.

additional_observations.observation: db/schema.rb in qa-run-2 includes unrelated AI feature tables
additional_observations.details: The schema.rb diff includes new tables (ai_api_requests, ai_credit_balance_transactions, ai_job_application_summaries, bulk_ai_summary_job_applications, organization_ai_credit_balances, organization_ai_credit_purchases) and a new column (auto_generate_ai_summaries_setting on jobs). These are from a separate feature branch that was merged into the base. The email-subjects-specific schema changes (subject on channel_messages, subject on channel_message_templates, mailgun_message_id on channel_messages, apply_response_template_subject on jobs) are all present and correct.

Line 307 of the diff has `font-size: ${t.text.sm};` which per pipeline known failure pattern #1 produces invalid CSS (double font-size declaration). This existed identically in qa-run-1 and is unchanged. Not a backend concern but noting for completeness since it appeared during review. This is a frontend issue for another reviewer to track.

summary: All 5 critical backend requirements are correctly implemented. The backend diff is byte-identical to qa-run-1. The only changes in qa-run-2 vs qa-run-1 are: (1) the ChannelMessageListItem.tsx frontend fix, and (2) db/schema.rb inclusion. No backend regressions, no spec deviations.
